title: NATO Spending Spreadsheet
text: A color-coded chart of which allies have reached 5 percent of GDP. Nobody has. Several are shaded a hopeful green.

options.label: Read every row
options.result: You learned that 3.5 plus 1.5 equals 5. You asked for the number to be bigger.

ignore.text: The chart went unread. Allies kept promising and you kept believing.

inspiredBy: NATO allies pledged 5 percent of GDP on defense by 2035 at the June 2025 Hague summit.

title: Greenland Working Group Minutes
text: Forty pages of minutes from talks with Denmark and Greenland. The word "purchase" appears zero times. The word "no" appears often.

options.label: Read the minutes
options.result: You finished. The island remains an island, and it remains not for sale.

ignore.text: The minutes stayed in the folder. The working group kept working without you.

inspiredBy: US, Danish and Greenlandic officials held working-group talks on Greenland from January 2026.

title: Trade Pact Review Binder
text: The review of the North American trade pact arrives as three binders, a flowchart and a glossary. Staff recommend the glossary first.

options.label: Study the flowchart
options.result: You traced a car part across three borders. It crossed seven times and got more expensive.

ignore.text: The binder gathered dust. The trade pact review went on without a view from the top.

inspiredBy: The US declined in July 2026 to extend the USMCA in its current form during the joint review.

title: Cables From Embassies
text: A stack of reports from ambassadors, many of them acting, some of them also acting as the cleaner. Each ends with a polite request for staff.

options.label: Read the cables
options.result: You learned that embassies exist in places you had only seen on tariff charts.

ignore.text: The cables went unread. Several embassies sent them again, louder.

inspiredBy: State Department cuts and a 2025 reorganization reduced diplomatic staff and strained embassies.

title: Foreign Aid Wind-Down Report
text: A report on which overseas programs were canceled, which were restored, and which no one can find. Appendix C is a shrug.

options.label: Go through the appendices
options.result: You found one program that worked. It had been canceled twice and reinstated once.

ignore.text: The report went unread. The shrug in Appendix C stayed unresolved.

inspiredBy: The administration dismantled USAID in 2025, with programs canceled and some later restored.

title: G20 Host Logistics Brief
text: The US hosts the G20 in December 2026 and staff want to discuss seating, motorcades, and which country gets the good chair. Your resort is mentioned eleven times.

options.label: Review the seating plan
options.result: You approved a seating plan. Nobody sat next to the empty South Africa chair.

ignore.text: The seating plan stayed undecided. Several leaders were seated near a fire exit.

inspiredBy: The US holds the 2026 G20 presidency, with the summit planned at a Doral golf resort in December.

title: A Very Large Gift Jet
text: A friendly government offers a luxury jumbo jet, free, no strings, definitely not a strings thing. Lawyers have used the word "emoluments" twice.

options.label: Politely pay for it
options.result: You offered to pay. The donor was baffled. Your lawyers brought a cake.

options.label: Accept the jet, wave from the stairs
options.result: You accepted. The jet is lovely and the hearing is scheduled.

ignore.text: The offer sat on your desk. The jet is still parked, looking expectant.

inspiredBy: Qatar offered a Boeing 747 for use as Air Force One in May 2025, prompting ethics objections.

title: Gift Crown, Slightly Used
text: A visiting ally presents a gold replica of an ancient royal crown. Protocol says it goes in the archive. The mirror says otherwise.

options.label: Send it to the archive
options.result: The crown went to the archive. You asked if it could be seen from there.

options.label: Try it on in the hallway
options.result: You tried it on. It fit perfectly, which is the problem.

ignore.text: The crown stayed in its box. The box got a plaque.

inspiredBy: South Korea gave a replica gold crown at the APEC summit in October 2025.

title: Executives Bring A Gold Bar
text: Business leaders from a tariffed country arrive with a gold bar and a luxury watch. They say it is "just a token." It is exactly the shape of a token.

options.label: Log it with the ethics office
options.result: The gifts were logged. An ethics lawyer held the bar and looked wistful.

options.label: Put the bar on the Resolute desk
options.result: The bar looked wonderful. The tariff rate went down eleven points.

ignore.text: The gold sat on the desk. The tariff talks sat next to it.

inspiredBy: Swiss business leaders gave Trump a gold bar and watch in August 2025 after US tariffs hit Switzerland.

title: The Board Of Peace
text: A new international council would be chaired by you, with permanent seats for a mere billion dollars. The charter is short. Your title is long.

options.label: Hand it to an independent body
options.result: You shared the chair. The charter now has footnotes and a vice chair.

options.label: Chair it yourself, permanently
options.result: You are chair for life. Several allies asked politely if they could not.

ignore.text: The charter stayed on your desk. The board met anyway and elected no one.

inspiredBy: Trump launched a Board of Peace in January 2026 with a $1 billion price for permanent membership.

title: The Canal Handover Idea
text: An aide suggests a calm arrangement with Panama over canal ports. You prefer the version with a flag, a parade, and your name on a lock.

options.label: Negotiate on port ownership
options.result: A calm deal was made. Ships went through. Nobody was named after anyone.

options.label: Demand the canal back, loudly
options.result: You demanded it. Panama said no in two languages and sent a map.

ignore.text: The canal question floated unanswered, like a very large boat.

inspiredBy: Trump pressed Panama over the canal and its ports from his January 2025 inauguration.

title: Fighter Jet For A Fan
text: A NATO ally you like would love some fighter jets. Another ally would love you not to. The sales brochure is shiny and says "friendship" twice.

options.label: Seek an allied consensus
options.result: You consulted. The allies agreed on a ratio of three objections to one hint.

options.label: Announce the sale on the spot
options.result: You announced it. Two allies learned about it from the television.

ignore.text: The jets stayed in the hangar. The brochure was reprinted.

inspiredBy: Trump said at the July 2026 Ankara NATO summit that Turkey could return to the F-35 program.

title: Spain Has Not Paid
text: One ally has declined the new 5 percent target. An adviser proposes a quiet, measured conversation. You propose a tariff with a name.

options.label: Hold a quiet conversation
options.result: The conversation was calm. Spain said "next year" in several tenses.

options.label: Threaten Spain with tariffs
options.result: You threatened Spain. Spain responded with a long lunch and no change.

ignore.text: The spending gap went unaddressed. Spain stayed on the shady side of the chart.

inspiredBy: Trump criticized Spain for refusing the 5 percent NATO spending target in 2025 and 2026.

title: Who Gets Invited To G20
text: You are hosting the G20, which means you pick the guest list. A country you dislike is on the guest list of a group that exists to include it.

options.label: Keep the usual invitations
options.result: You kept the list. The seating chart stayed the same. Nobody wrote a speech.

options.label: Strike a country from the list
options.result: You struck it. The host list is now shorter and your grudge is longer.

ignore.text: The guest list remained unsigned. Forty envelopes sat unlicked.

inspiredBy: Trump said South Africa would not be invited to the 2026 G20 after the US boycotted its 2025 summit.

title: The Big European Deal
text: A trade deal with Europe awaits signature. It has a 15 percent tariff, a promise of 750 billion dollars of energy, and a very vague word: "framework."

options.label: Get the numbers in writing
options.result: You asked for the numbers in writing. Brussels sent a larger document.

options.label: Declare the biggest deal ever
options.result: You announced a landmark deal. Europe spent the weekend reading it.

ignore.text: The deal stayed unsigned. Europe kept buying gas, and counting.

inspiredBy: The US and EU reached the Turnberry trade framework in July 2025 with a 15 percent tariff.

title: Ontario Ran An Ad
text: A provincial leader aired a television ad quoting a former president against tariffs. An aide says the talks could continue. You say they could not.

options.label: Keep the talks going
options.result: You stayed at the table. The ad ran another week, in your honor.

options.label: Cancel all talks, immediately
options.result: You canceled them. Canada watched the ad again on purpose.

ignore.text: The ad kept running. The talks lost the thread.

inspiredBy: Trump ended Canada trade talks in October 2025 after an Ontario anti-tariff ad quoting Ronald Reagan.

title: The Fifty-First State Call
text: A prime minister is on the line about tariffs. You would like to talk about statehood, stars on the flag and how nicely a map would look.

options.label: Stick to tariffs
options.result: You discussed tariffs. The prime minister thanked you and sighed in French.

options.label: Pitch statehood again
options.result: You pitched it. The prime minister said "no" the way an adult does.

ignore.text: You never called back. Canada took it as a refusal and a relief.

inspiredBy: Trump repeatedly floated making Canada the 51st state through 2025.

title: The No Strikes Call
text: A president calls to say Mexico will fight cartels on its own, thank you, and would rather not have your drones overhead. You have quite a lot of drones.

options.label: Agree to joint operations
options.result: You agreed to share intelligence. A general looked relieved, then suspicious.

options.label: Threaten land strikes in public
options.result: You threatened strikes on camera. Mexico pointed at its sovereignty and a map.

ignore.text: The call went to voicemail. The drones kept flying.

inspiredBy: Trump repeatedly threatened strikes on cartels on Mexican soil; Mexico refused in 2025 and 2026.

title: A Flattering NATO Chief
text: The NATO chief calls to say you will be an enormous success, and mentions that other leaders call you "daddy." The memo says this is a trick. It works.

options.label: Thank him and ask for spending
options.result: You asked for spending. He said yes to everything, in a tone you did not notice.

options.label: Believe every word
options.result: You believed it all. The communique was the length of a postcard.

ignore.text: You never called back. The NATO chief wrote the flattery in the communique anyway.

inspiredBy: NATO chief Mark Rutte flattered Trump around the June 2025 summit and used the word "daddy."

title: A Prime Minister Of Wine
text: The French president wants to talk tariffs on wine and everything else, before the dinner. You want to talk about the dinner.

options.label: Offer a measured tariff pause
options.result: You paused the tariffs. The French president said "merci" like a threat.

options.label: Threaten tariffs on his champagne
options.result: You threatened champagne. France stocked up on it and sent the invoice.

ignore.text: The call went unanswered. A pallet of wine started a retaliation list.

inspiredBy: Trump threatened new tariffs on France around the June 2026 G7 summit.

title: Denmark Is On Line One
text: The Danish prime minister is calling about the island, again. She will say the word "no" many times, kindly. You will say "ice" many times.

options.label: Discuss defense cooperation
options.result: You discussed radars. It was dull and she said it was the best call of her year.

options.label: Make an offer for the island
options.result: You made an offer. The offer was "no," but from your side.

ignore.text: You skipped the call. Denmark noted that you had skipped it and issued a statement.

inspiredBy: Trump kept pressing Denmark to cede control of Greenland through 2025 and 2026.

title: Security Guarantees, Again
text: The Ukrainian president wants security guarantees and a map that agrees with him. Your advisers want a ceasefire by Friday. You want applause.

options.label: Back a ceasefire with guarantees
options.result: You backed guarantees. The map shrugged, but a bit less than before.

options.label: Demand a deal by Friday
options.result: You demanded Friday. Friday arrived. Nothing else did.

ignore.text: The call was missed. The map went on being a map.

inspiredBy: Trump pressed Ukraine and Russia for a peace deal repeatedly in 2025 and 2026.

title: A Crown Prince With A Number
text: A crown prince offers an investment so large it needs a new unit. He mentions it casually, like a sandwich order. He does not mention human rights.

options.label: Ask about the human rights file
options.result: You asked. The pledge went down slightly and the sandwiches stayed.

options.label: Cheer the trillion
options.result: You cheered. The number grew again by the time you hung up.

ignore.text: The call was missed. The number was announced anyway.

inspiredBy: Saudi Arabia pledged hundreds of billions in US investment in 2025, later raised to near a trillion.

title: A Prime Minister Takes A Bow
text: A new prime minister calls to pledge 550 billion dollars of investment and to say how many times she admired you. Both numbers are large.

options.label: Ask for the investment details
options.result: You asked. She sent a binder with a plan and several friendly footnotes.

options.label: Say you are very proud of her
options.result: You said it. She said it back, with a gift.

ignore.text: The call went to voicemail. The prime minister left a very long, warm message.

inspiredBy: Japan pledged $550 billion in US investment in a 2025 trade deal; its new PM met Trump in Tokyo in October 2025.

title: The UN Escalator Incident
text: At the UN, the escalator stopped, the teleprompter stuck, and you have been asked to say a few words about it. A reporter has a microphone and a follow-up.

options.label: Say it was a technical glitch
options.result: You blamed a glitch. The UN said the escalator was not asked about your speech.

options.label: Call it a sabotage plot
options.result: You called for an investigation. Someone sent a janitor in a very small sweater.

ignore.text: You said nothing. The escalator story ran for three days.

inspiredBy: Trump said in September 2025 that a UN escalator and teleprompter failed during his visit.

title: Leaving The Summit Early
text: You are leaving a G7 early. A reporter asks if it was about the mood, the meeting or the lunch. A helicopter is waiting.

options.label: Stay and finish the session
options.result: You stayed. The leaders were thrilled, the lunch was fine and the helicopter was bored.

options.label: Leave early, praise yourself
options.result: You left. The communique was written without you and with your name in it.

ignore.text: You went to the helicopter. The G7 went on, politely refusing to mention you.

inspiredBy: Trump left the June 2025 G7 summit in Canada early, citing events in the Middle East.

title: The Davos Speech
text: You are addressing rich people in the Alps. They want to hear about economic cooperation. You have prepared a section on an island in the Arctic.

options.label: Stick to economic points
options.result: You stayed on message. The audience took notes, then went to a skiing event.

options.label: Talk about the island for forty minutes
options.result: You spoke about the island. The audience bought a few maps.

ignore.text: You did not speak. The Alps carried on, unbothered.

inspiredBy: Trump addressed Davos in January 2026 and used the speech to press for control of Greenland.

title: The Windsor Banquet Toast
text: A state banquet at a royal castle. A reporter asks for your thoughts on the day. The King has a very long sword and a very short patience.

options.label: Thank the host with grace
options.result: You thanked him gracefully. The King nodded with the restraint of a monument.

options.label: Mention the size of the castle
options.result: You said it was big, but yours was bigger. The room studied the tablecloth.

ignore.text: You spoke to no one. A footman refilled everything, in silence.

inspiredBy: Trump made a state visit to the UK in September 2025 with a banquet at Windsor Castle.

title: Dinner At Versailles
text: You are dining in a palace of mirrors and gold, hosted by a president. A reporter asks if the palace is a rival to your resort. It is.

options.label: Praise the host and the palace
options.result: You praised the palace. The gold lasted the whole dinner.

options.label: Say yours is better, with more gold
options.result: You said yours was better. A mirror caught the expression of the host.

ignore.text: You skipped questions. The mirrors reflected your empty chair.

inspiredBy: Trump dined with the French president at the Palace of Versailles after the June 2026 G7 summit.

title: The Peace Prize Question
text: A reporter asks whether you deserve the Nobel Peace Prize. You do, in your view. Several foreign leaders have said it too, in public, with enthusiasm.

options.label: Say the work matters more
options.result: You said the work mattered. The reporter asked if you meant it. You did, a bit.

options.label: List the wars you ended
options.result: You listed eight wars. A fact-checker wrote down eight question marks.

ignore.text: You did not answer. The foreign leaders kept nominating you in public.

inspiredBy: Foreign leaders publicly nominated Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize through 2025 and he repeatedly said he deserved it.
